node.title: Re: Question about tr (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Note that tr/// supports ranges, so this works too: tr|\0-9|A-Za-z|

(IIRC this might not work on systems that aren't ASCII based; [doc://perlebcdic])

Update: You said "the first 52 bytes of a character map", but \0-9 is the first 58 bytes. So maybe you want to do tr/\0-3/A-Za-z/? Or only the nonprintable characters with tr/\0-\x1F/A-Za-f/?

Update 2: [https://webperl.zero-g.net/democode/perleditor.html#%7B%22script%22%3A%22use%20warnings%3B%5Cnuse%20strict%3B%5Cn%5Cnprint%20join(%5C%22%20%20%20%5C%22%2C%5C%22%20%20%5C%22%2Cmap%20%7Bsprintf%20%5C%22%25X.%5C%22%2C%24_%7D%200..7)%2C%20%5C%22%5C%5Cn%5C%22%3B%5Cnfor%20my%20%24l%20(0..15)%20%7B%5Cn%5Ctprintf%20%5C%22.%25X%5C%22%2C%20%24l%3B%5Cn%5Ctfor%20my%20%24c%20(%20map%20%7B%20chr(%20%24l%7C(%24_%3C%3C%204)%20)%20%7D%200..7%20)%20%7B%5Cn%5Ct%5Ct%23%24c%20%3D~%20tr%2F%5C%5C0-9%2FA-Za-z%2F%3B%20%20%20%23%20doesn't%20work%20correctly!%5Cn%5Ct%5Ct%23%24c%20%3D~%20tr%2F%5C%5C0-3%2FA-Za-z%2F%3B%20%20%20%23%20option%201%5Cn%5Ct%5Ct%24c%20%3D~%20tr%2F%5C%5C0-%5C%5Cx1F%2FA-Za-f%2F%3B%20%23%20option%202%5Cn%5Ct%5Ctprint%20%5C%22%20%20%20%24c%20%5C%22%3B%5Cn%5Ct%7D%5Cn%5Ctprint%20%5C%22%5C%5Cn%5C%22%3B%5Cn%7D%5Cn%22%2C%22script_fn%22%3A%22ascii.pl%22%2C%22cmdline%22%3A%22perl%20ascii.pl%22%7D|WebPerl live demo of the following]:

use warnings; use strict; print join(" "," ",map {sprintf "%X.",$_} 0..7), "\n"; for my $l (0..15) { printf ".%X", $l; for my $c ( map { chr( $l|($_<<4) ) } 0..7 ) { #$c =~ tr/\0-9/A-Za-z/; # doesn't work correctly! #$c =~ tr/\0-3/A-Za-z/; # option 1 $c =~ tr/\0-\x1F/A-Za-f/; # option 2 print " $c "; } print "\n"; } __END__ 0. 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. 7. .0 A Q 0 @ P ` p .1 B R ! 1 A Q a q .2 C S " 2 B R b r .3 D T # 3 C S c s .4 E U $ 4 D T d t .5 F V % 5 E U e u .6 G W & 6 F V f v .7 H X ' 7 G W g w .8 I Y ( 8 H X h x .9 J Z ) 9 I Y i y .A K a * : J Z j z .B L b + ; K [ k { .C M c , < L \ l | .D N d - = M ] m } .E O e . > N ^ n ~ .F P f / ?
